Acupuncture involves the insertion of needles into specific locations on the body. These sites, known as acupuncture points, have been shown to relieve pain and improve health. Acupuncturists will often use moxibustion, massage (acupressure), or other methods that apply physical stimulation to the same points. The goal is to balance the flow of qi (vital energy) and thereby restore health.

If you suffer from migraines or headaches and are looking for alternatives to medications, talk to your doctor before embarking on any type of acupuncture therapy program. This is especially important if you take blood thinners, such as warfarin, heparin, or aspirin. Discuss your medical history with both your Western doctor and acupuncturist so that all aspects of care can be safely managed.

If you decide to try acupuncture, choose the most experienced and qualified acupuncturist you can find. A licensed acupuncturist must complete at least three years of education before sitting for a national board exam that qualifies them for state licensing.

There are few side effects associated with proper acupuncture, although there are some risks involved:
● Soreness, redness, pain, bruising, or bleeding at puncture sites
● Fainting, dizziness, or feelings of nausea
● Organ injury and punctured lungs
● Staph infections, dizziness, and fainting
● Broken needles
● Nerve damage
The risk of infection has decreased since acupuncturists now use new, disposable needles for each patient.

The number of treatments a person requires varies depending on their symptoms. Most individuals receive several treatments over two-three month periods. Some people continue regular acupuncture sessions to treat chronic conditions and improve overall health.

In one study, 62 people were given either traditional acupuncture or a placebo treatment and were asked about changes in how they felt after eight weeks. Those who received placebo acupuncture reported only small improvements in their migraines. But those receiving traditional acupuncture reported a statistically significant improvement in migraines.

If done by a professional acupuncturist, it would seem that acupuncture is likely to be helpful in the prevention of migraine headache. And it is certainly safer than many of the drug options used to prevent migraines.
